scope_notes: Full baseline of the local Juice Shop demo, including web server checks.

steps.reason: Template checks for common misconfigurations and technologies
Web server checks for additional security misconfigurations

plan.notes: The full baseline scope required running all selected tools for a thorough assessment.

execution.notes: All scans have been run as per the approved plan. The `nmap` scan discovered an open port, the `zap` scan identified several medium and low-risk issues, the `nuclei` scan found multiple informational and medium-risk findings, and the `nikto` scan, which timed out after 120 seconds, reported several potential security misconfigurations and interesting directories/files.

tool_runs.command: ZAP API: spider (max 1 min) + AJAX spider (60s) + passive scan of http://juice-shop:3000

nuclei -u http://juice-shop:3000 -jsonl -o /data/raw/eaee0d342f24445295dbb4aa098e1054/nuclei.jsonl -silent -no-color -disable-update-check -no-interactsh -omit-raw -rate-limit 50 -timeout 5 -retries 0 -exclude-tags intrusive,dos,fuzz,brute-force,default-login -t http/technologies -t http/misconfiguration -t http/exposures -t http/exposed-panels

tool_runs.note: Stopped at the 120s time box; results are partial.

executive_summary: The security posture of the system is concerning with multiple medium severity issues identified. The most critical issues include missing anti-clickjacking headers, content security policy, and session ID in URL. These should be addressed immediately to mitigate potential risks.

findings.title: Missing Anti-clickjacking Header
findings.description: The response does not protect against 'ClickJacking' attacks. It should include either Content-Security-Policy with 'frame-ancestors' directive or X-Frame-Options.
findings.remediation:
Modern Web browsers support the Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options HTTP headers. Ensure one of them is set on all web pages returned by your site/app.
If you expect the page to be framed only by pages on your server (e.g. it's part of a FRAMESET) then you'll want to use SAMEORIGIN, otherwise if you never expect the page to be framed, you should use DENY. Alternatively consider implementing Content Security Policy's "frame-ancestors" directive.
findings.severity_basis: zap rated it 'medium'; mapped to the matching CVSS band
findings.ai_remediation: Add the X-Frame-Options header to the response to prevent clickjacking attacks.

findings.title: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files.
findings.remediation: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.
findings.severity_basis: zap rated it 'medium'; mapped to the matching CVSS band
findings.ai_remediation: Implement a Content Security Policy (CSP) header to mitigate risks associated with inline scripts and other content.

findings.title: Cross-Domain Misconfiguration
findings.description: Web browser data loading may be possible, due to a Cross Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) misconfiguration on the web server.
findings.remediation:
Ensure that sensitive data is not available in an unauthenticated manner (using IP address white-listing, for instance).
Configure the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" HTTP header to a more restrictive set of domains, or remove all CORS headers entirely, to allow the web browser to enforce the Same Origin Policy (SOP) in a more restrictive manner.
findings.severity_basis: zap rated it 'medium'; mapped to the matching CVSS band
findings.ai_remediation: Review and secure the cross-domain configuration to prevent unauthorized access.

findings.title: Session ID in URL Rewrite
findings.description: URL rewrite is used to track user session ID. The session ID may be disclosed via cross-site referer header. In addition, the session ID might be stored in browser history or server logs.
findings.remediation: For secure content, put session ID in a cookie. To be even more secure consider using a combination of cookie and URL rewrite.
findings.severity_basis: zap rated it 'medium'; mapped to the matching CVSS band
findings.ai_remediation: Remove or obfuscate the session ID from the URL to prevent session hijacking.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
findings.description: The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'. This allows older versions of Internet Explorer and Chrome to perform MIME-sniffing on the response body, potentially causing the response body to be interpreted and displayed as a content type other than the declared content type. Current (early 2014) and legacy versions of Firefox will use the declared content type (if one is set), rather than performing MIME-sniffing.
findings.remediation:
Ensure that the application/web server sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all web pages.
If possible, ensure that the end user uses a standards-compliant and modern web browser that does not perform MIME-sniffing at all, or that can be directed by the web application/web server to not perform MIME-sniffing.
findings.severity_basis: zap rated it 'low'; mapped to the matching CVSS band

findings.title: Session Management Response Identified
findings.description: The given response has been identified as containing a session management token. The 'Other Info' field contains a set of header tokens that can be used in the Header Based Session Management Method. If the request is in a context which has a Session Management Method set to "Auto-Detect" then this rule will change the session management to use the tokens identified.
findings.remediation: This is an informational alert rather than a vulnerability and so there is nothing to fix.
